A LOOK INSIDE

Two ways to explore a recitation.

BEHIND THE EXPERIENCE

From sound to a meaningful match.

01

Recognize the reciter

An ECAPA-TDNN model creates a voice embedding. ONNX Runtime runs inference, then cosine similarity ranks matches against profiles for 20 reciters.

02

Find the verse

A Quran-tuned Whisper model transcribes the Arabic audio. Normalized text is matched against 6,236 verses to find likely surah and ayah matches.

03

Listen for more context

When a verse match is ambiguous, progressive listening gathers more audio context. Uncertain results stay marked as uncertain.

BUILT WITH

The technology behind it.

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS 4
  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • ONNX Runtime
  • faster-whisper
  • Docker
  • Render

Frontend: React 19 and TypeScript, built with Vite and Tailwind CSS 4. Browser microphone capture and file uploads connect to the API.

Backend: Python and FastAPI, with WebSockets for live reciter recognition. ONNX Runtime handles speaker embeddings; faster-whisper and CTranslate2 handle verse transcription.

Delivery: Docker containers on Render, with Nginx serving the frontend. GitHub Actions checks the backend and frontend before deploying affected services.

CHALLENGES & TRADEOFFS

Why it works this way.

Two questions, two pipelines

Recognizing a voice and recognizing words are different problems. Quranic Shazam uses ECAPA-TDNN speaker embeddings with ONNX Runtime to rank 20 reciter profiles. Verse discovery instead uses a Quran-tuned Whisper model, normalizes the Arabic transcript, and matches it against 6,236 verses. The speaker model is pretrained; it is not fine-tuned on Qur’an recordings.

Ask for context before claiming certainty

A short recitation can fit more than one verse. Progressive listening adds audio context up to a 60-second limit, while ambiguous results remain marked as uncertain. This trades a longer listening window for more context instead of forcing an early answer.

Measure a defined task

The September 5, 2026 offline evaluation reports 97.31% top-1 and 99.10% top-3 reciter recognition across 781 held-out clips, using disjoint profile and evaluation surahs. Those results describe that reciter benchmark; they do not measure verse recognition or guarantee performance on arbitrary microphones, noise, or recordings.
